newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Four killed in rebel attacks across Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in rebel attacks across Colombia.

text.p: Three soldiers and a civilian were killed in the latest flurry of leftist guerrilla attacks across Colombia, authorities said on Friday.

The soldiers died in an ambush by suspected National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels in the mountains of northern Cesar province, near the border with Venezuela, military officials said. Six troops were wounded in the attack.
A civilian contract worker for British Petroleum Co Plc was killed on Thursday night when rebels held up a convoy of oil workers in northeastern Casanare province.

Gen. Ismael Plata, commander of the Sixth Army Brigade, said masked rebels ordered workers to step down from six buses they were returning home in and set the vehicles ablaze. The worker killed had been travelling on a motorcycle and was shot as he tried to speed past the rebels roadblock.

In other developments, four policemen and a civilian were injured in a pre-dawn bomb attack on a police station that was reduced to rubble on Friday in Bello, a working-class district on the outskirts of the northwestern city of Medellin.
Police blamed the dynamite attack on urban commandos of the ELN or Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's leading guerrilla group.

FARC rebels were also believed responsible for torching two banana packing plants early on Friday in the violence-torn northwest region of Uraba, on the Caribbean coast near Colombia's border with Panama.
The FARC and ELN have both been waging war against the state since the 1960s.
